prose: Cory Doctorow's Pluralistic for 21 October argues adversarial interoperability is a team sport. Digital technology should be hard to enshittify because every computer is a Turing-complete universal machine: when a boss removes a valued feature (Sonos bricking speaker functionality) or adds a hated one (Chamberlain forcing seven ads before your garage door opens), a programmer can write an interoperable program that restores the good or blocks the bad, distribute it costlessly, and get paid for disenshittification. In a state of nature, that threat alone disciplines companies. His point in this edition: vibe-coded individual jailbreaks are fun but do not solve the structural problem; the counterpower has to be organized.
highlights: Adversarial interoperability is a team sport, not a solo jailbreak
Universal computers make enshittification technically reversible
Examples: Sonos feature removal, Chamberlain's seven garage-door ads
Disenshittification tools can be distributed costlessly and sold
Vibe-coded jailbreaks: fun, but structurally insufficient
